questions.stem: India's first National Park, established in 1936, is now known as:

options.option_text: Jim Corbett National Park (originally 'Hailey National Park')

questions.explanation: Established as Hailey National Park in 1936 (Uttarakhand) by United Provinces Governor Sir Malcolm Hailey. Renamed in 1957 after legendary hunter-turned-conservationist Jim Corbett. India's first National Park; also the launchpad of Project Tiger (1973). Located in Nainital and Pauri Garhwal districts, ~520 km². Major fauna — Bengal tigers, Asian elephants, leopards, ghariyals in River Ramganga.

questions.stem: Kaziranga National Park is famous for housing the world's largest population of:
questions.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam, on Brahmaputra floodplain) — UNESCO WHS 1985, declared NP in 1974, Tiger Reserve 2007. Home to ~2,613 Indian one-horned rhinos (2022 census), ~70% of the global population. Other 'Big Five': Asian elephant, wild water buffalo, Bengal tiger, Eastern swamp deer (state animal of Assam). Annual flooding from Brahmaputra is a natural recharge for grasslands but also a threat to wildlife crossing NH-37 to higher ground.

questions.stem: The only National Park in the world located within a major city's metropolitan limits is:
questions.explanation: Sanjay Gandhi NP (formerly Borivali NP) — 104 km² inside Mumbai's Greater Bombay area. Around 35-40 leopards live within metropolitan limits — the highest density in any urban-adjacent landscape worldwide. Houses the 2,400-year-old Kanheri Buddhist caves. Other distinctions: Hemis NP (Ladakh) — India's largest by area (~4,400 km²); Mahatma Gandhi Marine NP (A&N) — first Marine NP. There is no 'Indira Gandhi NP' in Delhi (that name applies to Pollachi-Anaimalai TR in TN).

questions.stem: Match the National Park with its state — which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Gir National Park is in GUJARAT — not Karnataka — Junagadh, Saurashtra region. Last home of the Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica), ~674 lions (2020 census). Bandhavgarh — MP, highest tiger density in India. Periyar — Kerala, around Periyar Lake, named after the river. Hemis — Ladakh, India's largest NP, snow leopard habitat. Karnataka's main NPs include Bandipur, Nagarahole, Bhadra, Anshi.

questions.stem: Sundarbans — a UNESCO World Heritage Site straddling India and Bangladesh — is most famous for:

options.option_text: Royal Bengal Tigers and the world's largest mangrove forest

questions.explanation: Sundarbans NP (West Bengal) — declared NP 1984, UNESCO WHS 1987. Contains the world's largest contiguous mangrove forest (~10,000 km² across India + Bangladesh). Home to 96 Bengal tigers (Indian portion, 2022 census) — these are unique 'salt-water tigers' that swim across creeks. Other species: estuarine crocodile, Gangetic dolphin, Olive Ridley turtles. Mangrove species — Heritiera fomes (sundari, the namesake), Avicennia, Rhizophora.

questions.stem: Project Tiger was launched in India in 1973. Its initial 9 tiger reserves did NOT include:
questions.explanation: Project Tiger inaugurated 1 April 1973, kicked off at Jim Corbett. Original 9 reserves: Corbett, Manas, Ranthambore, Palamau, Sariska, Kanha, Melghat, Bandipur, Sunderbans. Periyar added in 1978 (10th). India now has 58 Tiger Reserves (Mar 2025) covering ~75,000 km². Tiger count: 3,167 (2022 census, +6.7% over 2018). Ranthambore is famous for its 'royal cubs' visible from open jeeps; Bandipur for forest fires of 2019.

questions.stem: India's largest National Park by area is:
questions.explanation: Hemis NP — ~4,400 km² in eastern Ladakh. Home to ~200 snow leopards (highest density anywhere). Established 1981 to protect endangered Himalayan fauna — bharal (blue sheep), Tibetan wolf, Eurasian lynx, ibex. The Hemis monastery (1672) is within the park. India's smallest NP — South Button Island (Andaman & Nicobar) at 0.03 km².
